passage:
Many students signed up for a free online course, but only a few finished it.
A teacher asked why. Students said the course was interesting, but without a schedule, classmates, or teacher reminders, it was easy to stop.
They learned that access to learning materials is not the same as learning support.
The teacher helped them create study groups and weekly goals. More students completed the next course.
Online learning can open doors widely, but learners still need structure, feedback, and community. A library of videos is useful, but a path through them matters too.
